quoted_clause: so for $N=8$ the per-rank traffic is $1.75 \times 280 \approx 490$ GB and the sync time is $T_\text{ring} = 2\frac{N-1}{N}\,\text{bytes} / B_\text{eff}$. At 25 GB/s (single 200Gb/s link) that is `490 / 25 ≈ 19.6 s` per step ... At the H100 NVLink directional peak of 450 GB/s, the same ideal ring estimate is `490/450 ≈ 1.09 s`. The 900 GB/s bidirectional sum cannot divide a send-only traffic count
observed: The DP gradient-sync example counts 490 GB (= 2(N-1)/N × M = send + receive) and divides it by a *directional* bandwidth (450 GB/s, 25 GB/s). Ch 9 §3 Option A, for the identical eight-rank ring structure, counts 245 GB (send only) and divides by the same 450 GB/s directional peak, giving 0.54 s, and explicitly notes the equivalent form '490 GB of sent-plus-received traffic divided by 900 GB/s gives the same time'. Ch 10's own TP subsection uses the Ch 9 convention (send-only 448 KiB per call ÷ 450 GB/s). The DP subsection therefore mixes conventions within one chapter and contradicts Ch 9 by a factor of two.
correction: Restate the DP example in the Ch 9 convention: per-rank send volume = 2(N-1)/N × M = 490 GB is wrong as a 'send' figure — the send volume is 245 GB and the total (send+receive) is 490 GB. Then T_ring = 245 GB / B_dir: 245/450 ≈ 0.54 s at the H100 directional peak and 245/25 ≈ 9.8 s on a single 200 Gb/s link (or equivalently 490/900 and 490/50). Add one sentence defining 'per-rank traffic' once (send volume, receive volume, total) and reuse it in Ch 9, Ch 10 TP, Ch 10 DP, Ch 10 EP and Ch 10 FSDP. If the intent was to keep 490 GB, then the denominators must be the bidirectional figures (900 GB/s, 50 GB/s) and the printed results change accordingly.
acceptance_test: A single re-derivation script reproduces, for the same eight-rank ring and the same M, identical elapsed times in Ch 9 §3 Option A, Ch 10 TP, and Ch 10 DP; each printed time equals (send volume)/(directional bandwidth) with the direction convention stated in the same sentence.
verdict_fix: Restate DP send-only: 245/450≈0.54s, 245/25≈9.8s (or 490/900, 490/50); define 'per-rank traffic' once for ch09/ch10.
verdict_evidence: ch10:117 490/450=1.09s, 490/25=19.6s (send+recv over directional) vs ch09:98 245/450≈0.54s; ch10:117 itself says 900 GB/s 'cannot divide a send-only count'.
